turn_text: Hello. Good morning, sir. How are you? Very good. There's this new bill that you're introducing a paperwork reduction for farmers. Now, I'm ad-libbing there. Can you explain to us what this is?

Well, you know, a lot of Kentucky farmers have temporary workers that they use each season. And these are for jobs that are advertised for Americans to take. And we don't have enough people that are willing to work long hours in the hot sun. And so a lot of immigrant workers come through this program. When we talk to farmers, though, met some farmers who actually discovered that sometimes they wouldn't get their workers. They would have 17 workers one year and then the next year they'd apply for the same 17 workers and the government would just sort of sit on their application and not get it done and then They would lose an entire season or entire crop. And so we started looking at this program. It's called the H2A program. We started looking at ways that we could make it better by getting the government to respond to questions from farmers quicker to make the applications online, to allow the applications to be staggered so they don't all have to start at one certain date. And these are things that farmers said that would reduce red tape If workers have been coming each year for several years, they've been known to obey the law and be trustworthy, we make the process get sort of a heightened screening so it gets through the process quicker. So there's a lot of good things that we think we can do to this program to make it work better for the farmers. And then the final thing we did was we looked at whether or not you use somebody to help prepare you like a, you know, when you do your taxes, you hire somebody from the IRS. People who deal with this program often hire someone to help them do the paperwork. If you do that, you're trying to obey the law. We got rid of some of the criminal penalties because we found that there were people who were trying to obey the law that were found to have made a technical error somehow or the people they hired made a technical error and they were being accused of felonies with criminal sentences and we thought that was unfair for people who were trying to obey the law.
